record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: For a rational polygon P, let f_P(ℓ) be the number of periodic bands of length at most ℓ, and let c_*(P) and c^*(P) be constants giving quadratic lower and upper bounds c_*(P)ℓ^2 ≤ f_P(ℓ) ≤ c^*(P)ℓ^2 for all sufficiently large ℓ. Find effective estimates for these constants.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a rational polygon, that is, a simple polygon all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. Consider the billiard flow on $P$ (the geodesic flow obtained by free motion inside $P$ with elastic reflection at the boundary). A periodic billiard trajectory in $P$ is always part of a maximal family of parallel periodic trajectories of the same length, swept out by translating the trajectory perpendicular to its direction; such a maximal family is called a periodic band, and its length is the common length of the orbits in the family. For $\ell > 0$, let
$$f_P(\ell) = \#\{\text{periodic bands in } P \text{ of length} \le \ell\}.$$
It is known (Masur, Boshernitzan) that there exist constants $0 < c_*(P) \le c^*(P) < \infty$ such that
$$c_*(P)\,\ell^2 \;\le\; f_P(\ell) \;\le\; c^*(P)\,\ell^2$$
for all sufficiently large $\ell$. The problem is to give effective estimates for the constants $c_*(P)$ and $c^*(P)$, that is, explicit lower and upper bounds expressed in terms of the geometric data of $P$ (such as side lengths, angles, area, and the associated translation surface).
artifact.category_tag: Polygonal billiards and periodic orbit counting
artifact.status_search_result: Masur's original quadratic upper and lower bounds for the counting function of periodic bands (equivalently saddle connections / cylinders on the associated translation surface) were ineffective. Subsequent work, notably by Vorobets, has produced effective constant factors in some bounds, and there is continuing research on growth rates for geometric counting functions in polygonal billiards. Fully effective and sharp estimates of $c_*(P)$ and $c^*(P)$ in terms of the geometry of $P$ remain only partially achieved in general.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Masur established quadratic upper and lower bounds on the number of periodic cylinders/saddle connections of length at most L on translation surfaces; the original constants are not effective.
status_evidence.claim: Quadratic bounds exist but with ineffective constants in Masur's original argument.

status_evidence.title: Growth rates for geometric complexities and counting functions in polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Studies growth rates for geometric counting functions in polygonal billiards, with effective bounds in some settings.
status_evidence.claim: Effective bounds in restricted settings have been obtained, but a complete effective answer for general rational polygons remains open.

status_evidence.title: Super-fast spreading of billiard orbits in rational polygons and geodesics on translation surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on quantitative properties of orbits in rational polygons and translation surfaces, indicating ongoing activity in obtaining effective estimates.
status_evidence.claim: The area is active; effective constants in full generality are not yet established.
